reply.title: Why Does a Sigmoid Squash Any Number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When building models that make yes-or-no decisions, we often need to convert any numerical score into a probability between zero and one. If we use a simple linear rule, large inputs blow past our bounds. We need a smooth curve that gently bends to trap every possible input inside a finite ceiling and floor. This shape is the logistic sigmoid function. By adjusting its steepness, we control how rapidly the transition happens around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any real input into an output strictly between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness to see how sharply the curve transitions from flat to vertical.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to see how the curve changes shape. Observe the marker output update instantly.
